critical_code_review_comments: OK · Leased-slot semaphore replaces the counter-based Round-15 cap correctly: acquire/renew/release are token-fenced (foreign token no-op), lease expiry on crashed holders reclaims the slot proactively rather than waiting the old 30s stale window — hard-verified by TestRound16LeasedSlots.test_crashed_worker_lease_expires_and_slot_reclaimed and test_release_and_renew_are_token_fenced. This is a strict improvement over the Round-15 counter for pathological crash-loop resilience (previously flagged as OBSERVATION in iter-54).

OK · Per-account fairness cap (MAX_ACCOUNT_ACTIVE_SUBMISSIONS=2) and per-symbol fairness cap (MAX_SYMBOL_ACTIVE_SUBMISSIONS=3) prevent a single hot account/symbol from starving the 6-slot broker pool. Both caps exercised by dedicated tests (test_per_account_fairness_cap, test_per_symbol_fairness_cap) — passes cleanly.

OK · Pre-submit final-commitment edge revalidation (engine.py L880-906): after margin/exposure/slot acquire, the code re-reads a fresh quote, recomputes net edge with LATENCY_EDGE_BUFFER_PIPS deduction and rejects with reject_stage='pre_submit_edge_revalidation' if the trade would land below MIN_NET_EDGE_PIPS. Guards against the classic 'edge decayed while we were queuing' failure mode — exactly what a scalp path needs.

OK · Capacity rejections continue to carry dataset='attempt_not_submitted_capacity' so expectancy_by_mode.{shadow,broker_fills} strategy datasets are not polluted by infrastructure saturation events (verified in test_scalp_unit.py L2258).

OK · Regime dispatch pure logic in strategy_engines.dispatch_engine_for_regime: HIGH_VOL_TREND→mtf_relaxed, LOW_VOL_TREND→mtf_moderate, RANGE→range_fade, CHOP/unknown→stand-down HOLD. Fully covered by test_regime_dispatch.py (9 tests) including the previously-broken 'trending regimes dispatch to mtf cascades' path.

OK · REGIME_TO_PRESET fix in adaptive_mode.py — HIGH_VOL_TREND, RANGE, DYNAMIC_MOMENTUM, LOW_VOL_TREND labels no longer fall through to 'balanced'. Verified by TestAutoPresetRegimeTable.test_all_classify_regime_labels_mapped which asserts every classify_regime label has an explicit mapping (or an explicit block).

OK · 'adaptive' preset added as the FIRST item in strategy_presets.py order list so it's the default UI choice; ENGINE_BY_PRESET['adaptive']='regime_adaptive' correctly resolves to the dispatch engine. `POST /api/bot/preset/adaptive` preserves risk_level and symbols per spec — no accidental cross-writes.

OK · /api/scalp/metrics `expectancy_by_regime` block is keyed by regime LABEL (FLAT, TRENDING_DOWN today) with the same {n, net_expectancy_pips, ci95} shape as expectancy_by_mode — clients can pivot on regime with the same code path. Confidence intervals present even for small-n regimes (the ci95 field is always populated, either as a valid interval or as null for n=0).

OBSERVATION · expectancy_by_regime today only shows FLAT and TRENDING_DOWN because those are the only regimes the runner has actually decided on (EURUSD live). Once the runner sees HIGH_VOL_TREND / LOW_VOL_TREND / RANGE / CHOP labels in production, the endpoint will surface them automatically — no code change needed. Non-blocking.

OBSERVATION · The pre_submit_edge_revalidation reject_stage does not appear in the current unit-suite grep for test_scalp_unit.py; the code path is exercised indirectly through the mtf/scalp integration but a dedicated 'kill-the-edge-by-widening-spread-just-before-submit' unit test would nail down the LATENCY_EDGE_BUFFER_PIPS math. Non-blocking; consider adding as a TestRound17 seed test.

OBSERVATION · MAX_BROKER_CONCURRENT_SUBMISSIONS=6, MAX_ACCOUNT_ACTIVE_SUBMISSIONS=2, MAX_SYMBOL_ACTIVE_SUBMISSIONS=3 are all module-level constants — good for testability but a follow-up refactor could route these through env vars for per-deployment tuning (matches the pattern already used for MAX_BROKER_CONCURRENT_SUBMISSIONS which reads from env in Round 15).
